SURVEY_CS_TRANSFORMERS.paper_title: A Survey on Efficient Transformers, Linear Complexity, and Long-Context Architectures
SURVEY_CS_TRANSFORMERS.abstract: Standard self-attention scales quadratically with sequence length O(N^2), imposing fundamental memory and compute bottlenecks for long-context modeling. This survey systematically reviews advances in efficient transformer architectures, categorizing methods into IO-aware exact computation, rotary relative positional encodings, linear attention kernels, and KV-cache compression.

sections.heading: 1. Quadratic Attention Complexity & Hardware Memory Hierarchy
sections.text: The standard dot-product attention computes Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d))V. Materializing the full N-by-N attention matrix incurs O(N^2) time complexity and memory traffic. On modern accelerators like NVIDIA A100/H100 GPUs, standard attention is bottlenecked by memory-access latency between High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) and fast on-chip SRAM rather than raw FLOP compute throughput.

sections.heading: 2. IO-Aware Exact Attention & Tiling
sections.text: Rather than approximating attention via low-rank projections, IO-aware exact attention reorganizes execution into tiled blocks loaded into fast SRAM. By utilizing an online softmax scaling formulation, intermediate attention matrices S and P are never materialized to global HBM. Running statistics max(x) and sum(exp(x)) rescale accumulators dynamically on-chip, reducing HBM memory accesses by an order of magnitude while preserving exact mathematical equivalence to standard multi-head attention.

sections.heading: 3. Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE) and Relative Distances
sections.text: Absolute positional encodings fail to extrapolate to token sequences longer than pre-training windows. Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) resolves this by representing token positions via 2D rotation matrices applied to adjacent query and key vector coordinate pairs. The dot product between rotated vectors naturally incorporates relative distance (m - n), with the inner-product magnitude decaying gracefully as distance increases.

sections.heading: 4. KV-Cache Compression and Multi-Query Attention
sections.text: During autoregressive token generation, caching Key and Value states consumes massive GPU VRAM proportional to batch size, number of heads, hidden dimension, and context length. Multi-Query Attention (MQA) and Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) reduce KV-cache memory footprints by sharing a single key-value head across all query heads or subgroups of query heads, yielding up to an 8x reduction in decoding memory overhead.

sections.heading: 5. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Integration
sections.text: To bypass context length constraints entirely, RAG architectures decompose knowledge management into parametric language models and non-parametric vector indices. External evidence passages are retrieved via dense bi-encoders and reciprocal rank fusion, packing relevant evidence snippets dynamically into the prompt.

SURVEY_BIO_STRUCTURAL.paper_title: Deep Learning for Macromolecular Modeling and 3D Protein Structure Prediction: A Comprehensive Survey
SURVEY_BIO_STRUCTURAL.abstract: Predicting the three-dimensional atomic structure of macromolecules from linear sequences has been a foundational challenge in biophysics. This survey reviews deep learning architectures in structural biology, highlighting multiple sequence alignment processing, SE(3)-equivariant coordinate updates, and diffusion-based protein design.

sections.heading: 1. Evolutionary Covariance and Multiple Sequence Alignments
sections.text: Homologous protein sequences across evolutionary history mutate under spatial constraints. When two residues are in direct physical contact in 3D space, a mutation in one residue is compensated by a correlated mutation in the interacting residue. Multiple Sequence Alignments (MSAs) encode these statistical covariances across species.

sections.heading: 2. Evoformer Representations and Invariant Point Attention
sections.text: Modern structure prediction networks like AlphaFold2 operate on dual representations: an MSA representation and a spatial pair representation. The structure module places each residue into an independent SE(3) rigid body frame. Invariant Point Attention (IPA) computes scalar attention alongside 3D Euclidean coordinate points in local frames, guaranteeing complete rotational and translational invariance without requiring explicit coordinate alignment.

sections.heading: 3. Unsupervised Protein Language Models (pLMs)
sections.text: While MSA-based models require extensive homology search against sequence databases, protein language models (such as ESM) train transformer encoders on billions of unaligned amino acid sequences via masked token prediction. Attention contact maps within ESM capture secondary structure and tertiary contact probabilities in zero-shot regimes.

sections.heading: 4. Diffusion Models for De Novo Macromolecular Design
sections.text: Beyond predicting natural proteins, generative SE(3) diffusion models construct novel protein backbones from scratch. Continuous score-based diffusion operates on SO(3) rotations and R^3 translations, generating diverse functional scaffolds for targeted binder design and catalytic enzyme engineering.

SURVEY_SYS_CONSENSUS.paper_title: Fault-Tolerant Consensus Protocols in Distributed Databases and Storage Systems: A Systematic Review
SURVEY_SYS_CONSENSUS.abstract: Maintaining replicated state consistency across asynchronous networks subject to node crashes and packet drops is central to distributed storage. This review analyzes crash-fault-tolerant (CFT) protocols, contrasting Paxos and Raft, and discusses log compaction and linearizable read optimizations.

sections.heading: 1. Replicated State Machine Architecture
sections.text: Replicated state machines enforce consistency by ensuring that all healthy replicas execute an identical log of state machine operations in identical sequence. The consensus protocol guarantees safety (agreement on log entries) and liveness (progress as long as a strict majority of nodes 2f + 1 remain non-faulty).

sections.heading: 2. Paxos Deconstruction vs. Raft Understandability
sections.text: Multi-Paxos decomposes consensus into asymmetric roles of Proposers, Acceptors, and Learners. Raft was developed to resolve Paxos implementation opacity by decomposing consensus into three independent sub-problems: leader election, log replication, and safety invariants. Leaders are elected using randomized election timers, and log completeness ensures that a newly elected leader already contains all previously committed log entries.

sections.heading: 3. Linearizable Read Optimizations & Leader Leases
sections.text: Routing read queries through the consensus write log incurs heavy disk IO and round-trip latency. To serve linearizable reads without writing to disk, leaders utilize leader leases (synchronized clock intervals) or ReadIndex rounds (confirming current leadership via a heartbeat quorum before returning read results).

sections.heading: 4. Log Compaction and Snapshotting
sections.text: As distributed transactions accumulate indefinitely, servers cannot retain complete transaction histories in memory. Log compaction periodically writes a point-in-time snapshot of the state machine to non-volatile disk and truncates all preceding log entries, transferring snapshot chunks over RPC only to severely lagged or newly joined replicas.

SURVEY_AI_AGENTS.paper_title: A Comprehensive Survey of Autonomous LLM Agents: Tool Use, Memory Systems, and Planning
SURVEY_AI_AGENTS.abstract: Autonomous agents powered by Large Language Models integrate reasoning, tool calling, and long-term memory to execute multi-step workflows. This survey categorizes agent architectures across memory hierarchies, iterative planning mechanisms, and execution environments.

sections.heading: 1. Cognitive Agent Architectures
sections.text: Autonomous agent systems augment foundation models with three core modules: planning (decomposing goals into tasks), memory (storing past observations and reflections), and tool use (executing APIs, shell commands, and code interpreters).

sections.heading: 2. Memory Architectures: Short-Term vs. Vector Long-Term
sections.text: Short-term memory manages in-context prompt scratchpads and conversation history bounded by the context window. Long-term memory persists experiential knowledge across sessions using external vector databases. Memories are indexed by recency, importance, and semantic relevance, retrieving top historical experiences on demand.

sections.heading: 3. Reasoning and Planning Frameworks
sections.text: Pioneering planning frameworks like ReAct interleave reasoning traces with domain actions in a Thought-Action-Observation loop. Tree-of-Thoughts (ToT) expands deliberate search by exploring multiple reasoning trajectories with heuristic evaluation, while Reflexion reinforces task execution through self-reflective critique and persistent failure memory buffers.

sections.heading: 4. Tool Use and External Environment Execution
sections.text: Agents interact with computational environments by generating structured function calls (JSON schemas) executed via sandbox runtimes. Sandbox isolation prevents unauthorized filesystem modifications and network access while parsing output streams.
